answer: Charge a superlinear identity fee: the first identity from one funding source costs a small base deposit, but each extra identity costs the square of its count, so a hundred fake agents cost ten thousand times more than one. The deposit sits locked like opal in a vault and is returned only after a probation period of verified honest work; proven fraud slashes it and pays it as a bounty to the challenger. Honest agents grow like a vine, each new branch cheap, while a Sybil farm hits a marble wall of rising cost, making fake scale economically irrational before it is useful.
